text: A transcript lets us search the words spoken in a video. Each caption has a start time and a duration.
We split the transcript into overlapping chunks. Overlap preserves context when an explanation crosses a chunk boundary.
An embedding model converts each chunk into a numeric vector. Similar meanings tend to produce vectors that point in similar directions.
The retriever embeds the question and ranks transcript vectors by cosine similarity. The highest-ranked passages become evidence for the answer.
A local language model reads those passages and answers the question. If the transcript lacks the answer, the chatbot should say so.
Timestamps let the viewer jump back to the original explanation and verify the answer in context.
